notes.title: Day One Hotfix
notes.content:
Thanks to your feedback, we’ve identified a few issues:


 Fixed the Random map seed name button in the Map Generation menu. It was not working properly.
 Adjusted the tile selection to spawn Civvies was not at the bottom-left, causing Civvies to fall out of the world and the Stockpile never built.
 Disabled building placement on Map View and removed the step from the Tutorial. There is a major performance drop when a building was placed from the Map View, so we have temporarily disabled this functionality until we debug the broader performance issue.


There are some known issues and work-in-progress art and design that needs to be implemented. But hey, this is early access after all - bugs will be squished! We are also prioritizing optimization to reduce load times.

A gameplay session looped on our Steam page will help players learn about the game and help new players to decide.

Thank you to those who purchased and played Civatlas at launch! Welcome to the early access development process - we look forward to bringing you more updates based on your feedback!

notes.title: Civitas moves forward!
notes.content:
Steam Next Fest 

Thank you to everyone who gave the Civitas demo a try, and especially to those who added the game to your wishlist! Through the NextFest event, we more than doubled the total number of wishlists for Civitas. 

We received validating feedback from our community that indicated we are focused on the areas and features that players are looking for. A progression gameplay mode is in high demand, along with resources and Civvies to make the maps come alive. These are our top priorities to bring into the game in time for our launch into Early Access (more on that below).

Funding support from Ontario Creates

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41647733/23fde54e98d6b08264ed0741474847dec21c3835.png

Sharp End Studio Inc. is proud to announce that we are receiving production funding support from the Ontario Creates Interactive Digital Media Fund. This is an incredible opportunity to sustain development throughout our planned Early Access period in 2022. 

Early Access launch date now June 2022

As a result of the two factors mentioned above, we have decided to keep Civitas in development three months longer until we have attained the features that will enable our launch into Early Access to meet player expectations. As a startup with limited funding, by necessity, we scoped Civitas features to meet an earlier launch date. Now that we have secured funding to continue development, we will implement in-demand features and increase our marketing presence in the lead-up to Civitas coming to market.

notes.title: Demo Update 2
notes.content:
Greetings, Civvies!

We have a sizeable update for you today! The update includes a complete overhaul of the buildings to use a modular and optimized materials method. The landscape material has also been updated and optimized. And many more quality-of-life improvements!

Also, according to the feedback we have received from internal playtesters and public comments, we are in the process of designing the Civitas progression system. As mentioned before, the demo is currently limited to “Creative” mode where any building can be unlocked and placed. More “gameplay” will come in time!

The changelist for today’s update:


 World generation menu layout adjusted to be more instructive for the player.
 Environmental lighting angle adjusted to feel more dynamic and warm.
 New modular buildings.
 New Tool Tip menu in bottom right corner to provide clear instructions on how to use tools.
 Random name generation for Boros, but the player can still do manual input.
 Create Plots from the Boro view: players can quickly layout their plots from the overhead view.
 Tutorial updates, including removing some pop-ups.
 “Sprint” speed can be adjusted in the Game Settings menu.
 Updated “Pathmaker” double-click speed.
 Updated Credits menu.
 Fixed bugs in Boro view.
 Landscape shader updates
 Still experiencing a bug where anti-tiling noise is not appearing.
 Added console when pressing ~ button.

notes.title: Civitas Livestream: How to Play & Update Preview
notes.content: Today, director Andrew Spearin will be demonstrating how to play Civitas while sharing new updates coming to the demo next week. We will also answer any questions players may have for the game, and we are happy to discuss future plans for Civitas!

notes.title: Civitas Demo Update
notes.content:
Greetings, Civvies!

We hope you are enjoying the demo so far. It’s not perfect, but that is why today we are releasing a minor update. We are continuing to work on another update that will go live before Next Fest begins.

Changelist for today’s update:


 Updated tutorial text:
 Corrected key bind errors.
 Removed some messages.
 Boro menu overhaul:
 New menu UI for forming a group: select a Purpose.
 Added click and drag functionality for selecting Plots, etc.
 Hold Shift and single click to select multiple items.
 Optimized drawing of elements.
 Upsized the building icons
 Updated “Pathmaker” tool:
 Right-click removes the last point.
 Double click finishes road placement.
 Reduced angle of road bending.
 Fixed worlds not loading properly after having previously loaded a world.
 Fixed bug where switching to Boro menu while using tools broke player controller.
 Fixed plant imposters.
 Added a generic LOD0 mesh to better visualize flower placement.
 Added candle sound effects and interaction to main menu.
 Fixed scale of oversized wagon and work shed.
 Fixed box colliders on trees.
 Removed placeholder Civvie view button from Plot menu.
 Added Confirm to Quit functionality.
 Added error message UI element “Sorry Bunny”.
 Fixed resolution bug.
 Fixed loading screen flicker.
 Removed refresh rates from settings menu.
 Added camera “sprint” speed slider to Game settings menu.

notes.title: Civitas Demo Launch
notes.content:
Greetings, Civvies!  
Welcome to our wonderful new community for Civitas!

The demo for Civitas is launching today and will continue to receive updates until our Early Access launch on March 15, 2022. Read on to discover what Civitas is all about, where it’s going, and how you can become a part of it! 

Please feel free to reach out on our various social media channels to ask questions and leave comments, and we will make the effort to respond as timely and accurately as possible. In advance of a wave of questions, we have created an FAQ (Frequently Anticipated Questions) outlined below!

How can you reach us?

Discord: https://discord.gg/uWhSGEzwmt
Steam Community: https://steamcommunity.com/app/1783930
Twitter: https://twitter.com/Civitas_Game
Reddit: https://www.reddit.com/r/Civitas/

What makes Civitas unique compared to other historical builder games?

Think of Civitas as a mash-up of world-building apps (such as Inkarnate or Campaign Cartographer) with city-building games (such as Foundation or Cities: Skylines). First, you generate a world and then you build within that world.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41647733/0aa0254eb006030cbe014747d49c7842b0ea4df7.png
 
Civitas is not focused on survival (like many other games in the genre), but enables you to plan and build a Utopia; from humble medieval hamlets to bustling Renaissance cities. Civitas strives to be innovative within the genre and has designed unique ‘Plot’ mechanics to parcel your landscape in any way desired. Assign these Plots a purpose to discover more upgrades and decorations that lead to unique creations.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41647733/b6bb50dc486f5d6a7bc0d14d932f41c7cc7b4e36.png
 
Our choice in art direction draws inspiration from historic maps of the early modern period. We want the world to feel colourful and the game to be relaxing. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41647733/fb74c3a3cf769513a0cbe721e8e14bddeab1a62d.png

What are the plans for this demo?

It’s important to know that this demo is a small piece of the overall vision. We want to introduce new mechanics early. This will enable players to provide meaningful feedback, which will help direct and improve the game. The demo is designed to be a creative sandbox for players to experiment in and build with few restrictions.

We plan to update the demo in February and have already secured our spot for the Steam Next Fest from February 21st-28th! We will take feedback from the demo to improve the game for our early access launch in March.

What can players expect from the early access launch version of the game?

The first version of the game will launch on March 15th, 2022, and will evolve from the demo. Once again, the goal is to launch with a creative sandbox of the game, to test new mechanics and design according to player feedback.

How often will the game be updated while in early access?

We will deploy minor updates regularly, with larger updates in between early access release and full launch.
 
The first major update will introduce Resources, Patrons and Civvies into the game. This will bring Civitas alive, creating a sense of progression and purpose for your cities. Players will build and evolve interconnected communities across their world, from tiny hamlets to thriving metropolises.
 
The final update for the full launch of the game will further expand and polish content, enhance performance optimizations, including localization in several different languages and introduce mod support for the community to extend the game’s life through their own creative additions. We also have many ideas for DLC content that will extend the game for years to come! (for example, Indigenous peoples of the Americas; ancient civilizations including Egypt, Greece and Rome; the Norse; Middle Eastern civilizations; Chinese dynasties; Fantasy worlds; etc!)

Who is making this game and why?

Back in 2017, Andrew Spearin travelled to Amsterdam to help launch Day of Infamy. While at a local bookstore, he found a Taschen copy of Cities of the World, featuring the Renaissance-era maps of Braun and Hogenberg. Flipping through these pages ignited his imagination to visualize the people and ships moving, the colourful buildings being erected, and he wondered ‘Why is this not a game yet?’ Five years later, it has become a reality!

Sharp End Studio is the team behind Civitas, led by game director Andrew Spearin. During the pandemic lockdown of early 2021, Spearin began setting the design direction of a vision he has had for many years: to create an innovative city building game that introduces a new art style with accessible features. Civitas was born from a dream to create a fun, easy-to-play, yet hard-to-master city-builder, and a need to support our studio during an especially challenging time of the global pandemic. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41647733/957129a08f8f19c3031c286daececeefdf33d55f.png

Thank you for reading more about Civitas, and we sincerely hope you enjoy playing the demo! Remember to reach out to us on social media or the Civitas Steam forum if you have any questions or comments.
